title: DiOffice
subtitle: Virtual Software Company for AI Employees
shortDescription: A virtual software company where an Owner manages permanent AI employees — identity and history persist while agent runtimes stay swappable.
longDescription: DiOffice is an experiment in durable AI teamwork: a virtual software company where an Owner manages permanent AI employees. Employee identity and work history are persistent; the runtime — OpenCode first — is a replaceable tool behind a gateway. The v0.1 target is one honest end-to-end flow: task drafts, explicit start, isolated workspace, real repository work, checks and preview evidence bound to a commit SHA, PR review, approval, and merge — with a pixel-office UI driven only by real backend state.
problem: Most AI-coding tools show output, not work — there is no persistent employee identity, no auditable event trail, and UI progress is often simulated rather than backed by real state.
solution: An event-sourced office: every employee action becomes a normalized durable event, task state machines are explicit (DRAFT → BACKLOG/READY → DONE, with merge as a separate Owner action), and the pixel-office UI renders only real backend state — never simulated progress.
responsibilities: Authored the product spec — state machines, event schema, execution manifest, user flows
Built the Go API — session/CSRF auth, task and event endpoints, explicit migrations
Built the React + Vite shell with a Phaser pixel-office layer
Defined the agent-gateway boundary (Node.js) and the first runtime adapter (OpenCode)
Specified execution isolation — Docker + git worktree, Temporal for workflow durability
features: Persistent AI employees with identity and work history
Explicit task lifecycle — Owner gates every transition
Normalized event stream with durable SSE replay cursor
Evidence-bound reviews — checks and previews tied to the tested commit SHA
Pixel-office UI rendered from real backend state

decisions.title: No simulated work
decisions.rationale: Character animation, monitors, diffs, tests, and progress must come from real task/runtime events — nothing fake.

decisions.title: Persistent identity, swappable runtime
decisions.rationale: Employees keep identity and history; runtimes like OpenCode are replaceable tools behind the gateway.

decisions.title: Owner-in-the-loop
decisions.rationale: Start, approve, and merge are explicit Owner actions — the AI never merges its own work.

impact: Working foundation — Go API with auth and task drafts, React shell, agent-gateway health endpoint, executable migrations
